subject: APAC region data residency waiver and routing exception — StratoHealth request
messages:
From: Kamala Rao <kamala@stratohealth.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 09:14:00 +0800
Subject: Request: APAC-only routing + no-fallback for regulated workflows

Hi Elliot,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — StratoHealth is moving quickly on the patient-facing summarization flow. Our legal and privacy teams have flagged a hard requirement for a short-term data residency guarantee while we finish certification: all inference for the production integration must execute in the Singapore region (apac-sg) and there must be no automatic fallback to any other region or variant that could process payloads outside APAC.

We understand that this is operationally unusual; we want to discuss a time-bound waiver (30 days to start, with the possibility to extend) and capture the change in the SOW. Could you confirm whether Redwood can: 1) bind requests for our account to APAC-only hosts; and 2) disable automated cross-region fallback for our tenant for this window?

We are happy to sign an amendment and accept a documented availability/latency tradeoff, but compliance is non-negotiable for this phase. Attaching the compliance note from our side in a follow-up.

Best,
Kamala
Director, Product & Privacy
StratoHealth
From: Elliot Price <elliot@redwood.com>
To: Kamala Rao <kamala@stratohealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 10:02:00 +0800
Subject: Re: Request: APAC-only routing + no-fallback for regulated workflows

Hi Kamala — thanks for the clear ask and for surfacing the compliance requirement.

Short answer: we can implement an APAC routing rule for your account and we can limit automated fallback behaviors for a defined window, but there are trade-offs I want to make explicit so your security/compliance team understands them:

- Availability: removing automatic fallback increases risk of user-facing errors during regional outages.
- Performance: in some failure modes we may not be able to meet latency SLOs.
- Operational escalation: we will need a manual runbook to fail over if APAC capacity is saturated.

Can you confirm target start date and minimum waiver window (you mentioned 30 days)? Also, do you require customer-managed KMS for model inputs/outputs? If so we need early coordination.

Looping in Karthik to scope the engineering approach and Laura for legal amendment language. Monica will queue the amendment and MLP so we can turn this into a signed change.

Thanks,
Elliot
Senior Manager, Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot@redwood.com>, Kamala Rao <kamala@stratohealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 12:37:00 +0800
Subject: Re: Request: APAC-only routing + no-fallback for regulated workflows

Elliot / Kamala — technical note from the serving/runtime side:

- We can create a tenant-level routing policy that pins all inference to the apac-sg pool. That is straightforward.
- "No automatic fallback" is trickier: our platform has automated fallback for capacity and model-compatibility reasons. We can disable the automated cross-region fallback for your tenant for a bounded window (we typically do this via a feature flag + policy gate).
- Constraints and recommended mitigations:
  * We recommend a 14-day technical trial before a 30-day production window — this allows us to identify latent capacity bottlenecks with real traffic.
  * Require a held capacity reservation or burst commit for the window — otherwise we cannot guarantee successful delivery under peak.
  * Customer-managed KMS: if StratoHealth provides a KMS key and mandates encrypt-at-rest with a key accessible only in APAC, we can ensure backups/replicas used for hot-failover stay encrypted and unreadable outside the region.

Operationally we will: open SUP-2134 to track the engineering work (https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-2134), create a runbook page (https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/APAC+No-Fallback+Runbook), and expose a manual failover action for our on-call.

Two asks from you for us to proceed: 1) confirm commitment to a reserved capacity level (TBD), and 2) confirm whether StratoHealth will supply a KMS key or accept our managed key with contractual limitations.

-Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Hi Kamala — thanks, we’ve drafted a short Mutual Action Plan and an SOW amendment that captures the routing exception, the no-automatic-fallback clause, and the reserved capacity commitment. I’ve attached:

- mutual_action_plan.pdf (summary timeline and milestones)
- apac_no_fallback_sow.docx (contract amendment draft)
- redlines_contract_v2.pdf (our proposed redlines)

Key commercial bullets:
- Initial trial: 14 days technical validation + 30 day production waiver (subject to agreed reserved capacity).
- Pricing: a temporary reserved-capacity uplift during the waiver window (detailed in attachment).
- Sign-off: legal amendment + DocuSign required before we flip the no-fallback flag.

Next step: can you confirm whether StratoHealth will provide a KMS key (we include instructions in the runbook) or if you prefer Redwood-managed keys with contractual restrictions? If you can sign the DocuSign link we’ll schedule engineering to enact the routing policy the week after sign.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 11:42:00 +08:00
Subject: Re: Request: APAC-only routing + no-fallback for regulated workflows — legal conditions

Team — quick legal sign-off with conditions:

1) Approve subject to signed amendment that: 1a) explicitly documents availability trade-offs and attaches the runbook; 1b) includes an indemnity carveout for third-party regulatory claims; and 1c) limits the waiver to an initial 30-day window (extension by mutual written agreement).
2) KMS requirement: if StratoHealth wants a legally enforceable guarantee that plaintext never leaves APAC, we must use a customer-controlled KMS key with per-region key material and proof-of-possession controls. We should not accept a purely contractual promise in lieu of a technical KMS control.
3) Security evidence: require the SOC2 snapshot and the PoP for the KMS before flip.

If Monica gets the signed amendment and the KMS token material we can greenlight engineering to flip the flag (Karthik: please keep the manual failover button gated by legal approvals).

-Laura
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
